events.text: Hyde vanishes after Sir Danvers's murder; rewards are offered.
events.quote: thousands of pounds were offered in reward, for the death of Sir Danvers was resented as a public injury

events.text: Jekyll emerges from seclusion and resumes his old friendships.
events.quote: He came out of his seclusion, renewed relations with his friends

events.text: Utterson dines with Jekyll and Lanyon as inseparable friends.
Jekyll shuts his door against Utterson, Poole reporting he is confined.
events.quote: the door was shut against the lawyer

events.text: Utterson visits Lanyon and is shocked by his decayed appearance.
events.quote: he was shocked at the change which had taken place in the doctor’s appearance

events.text: Lanyon declares himself a doomed man who will never recover.
Lanyon refuses to hear Jekyll's name, calling him dead to him.
events.quote: I wish to see or hear no more of Dr. Jekyll

events.text: Utterson writes to Jekyll, who replies of an incurable quarrel.
events.quote: Utterson sat down and wrote to Jekyll

events.text: Jekyll vows extreme seclusion and speaks of an unnameable punishment.
events.quote: I mean from henceforth to lead a life of extreme seclusion

events.text: Lanyon takes to his bed and dies within a fortnight.
events.quote: Dr. Lanyon took to his bed, and in something less than a fortnight he was dead

events.text: After the funeral Utterson opens Lanyon's sealed envelope.
events.quote: Utterson locked the door of his business room

events.text: The enclosure is not to be opened till Jekyll's death or disappearance.
events.quote: not to be opened till the death or disappearance of Dr. Henry Jekyll

events.text: Utterson prefers speaking with Poole at the door rather than entering.
events.quote: he preferred to speak with Poole upon the doorstep

events.text: Poole reports Jekyll confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.
events.quote: now more than ever confined himself to the cabinet over the laboratory
